posts.fullCaption: This interesting to think about… but I don’t think it’s completely accurate or true across the board. I think constant, new information just leads us to new perspectives… and the things we no longer wonder about go away, while we just create new things to wonder about. I feel like the mind is just malleable to whatever environment it’s in. Some things can very much be a distraction… but other things can also lead us think and imagine even more. If anything… we can blame our systems as a whole for mundane cyclical activities like scrolling. Some people might even view doing that as boring. But depending on what the mind is actually hungry for, it can also be just as much of a thought “adventure”. Pertaining to our systems, I think schools also put us in a state that lacks creativity. Curriculum just teaches us to regurgitate information over and over again. We learn basic ideas that don’t nurture or cultivate creativity. The world is also seemingly smaller as cultures blend more and people travel much more frequently. There feels like there is a constant change in perspective for some people. I think all of these things are purely dependent upon the person and their actual intent in life. But I can definitely see this being a perspective of different individuals. There is most certainly a mode of mindless scrolling. But there are also very intentional activities. There are also the factors of these cyclical natures that we create of waking up, going to work, supporting our vices, going to sleep… then doing it all over again almost every single day. A lot of jobs have resulted in a lot of people being overworked and underpaid… I just feel like there’s way more to a lot of things and blaming the lack of those “empty spaces” on doom scrolling alone is such a cop out way to view things.

posts.fullCaption: unfoldedai 20 wOpenAI and Anthropic engineers revealed the prompt techniques they use through internal documents.What stands out is how different their approach is from how most people use AI. Prompting is not treated as clever wording or guesswork, but as system design built around structure, constraints, and controlled behavior.Instead of relying on vague instructions, they define strict rules that limit what the model can and cannot do. Instead of writing one long request, they break complex tasks into smaller steps that validate each other before moving forward. Instead of hoping the format stays consistent, they enforce structure so outputs remain reliable every time.They also separate system rules from user input to keep behavior consistent, adjust temperature based on the type of task, and add self checks before the final answer is returned.The goal is not to sound impressive. The goal is to reduce errors, increase first pass success, and produce results teams can actually trust.Across real workflows, these patterns lead to measurable improvements in quality, consistency, and time saved. The gap is not model intelligence. The gap is prompt discipline.What are your thoughts on this? 🤔💬Follow for more @unfoldedai#ai #automation #tech #ainews #aitools

posts.fullCaption: liamottleyVerified Edited•9 wThe past 2 months in AI have been the wildest I have seen in over 3 years of actively building in the space. If you’re a founder wondering where this is all going, here’s all you need to know: 1) In ~5 years, most businesses will run on an AI operating system, or AIOS for short. 2) An AIOS is based around one central AI that knows your whole business, plugged into all your tools and data sources. You and your team work from inside it. 3) We have primitive versions of these already using Claude Code. I’ve been helping other founders set them up via both in person masterminds and through my program. The shift in speed of execution for tasks and projects is insane. 4) An AIOS starts with context. Export your ChatGPT or Claude chats and feed it in. Tell the AI your strategy, your team, your priorities once and you’ll never have to tell it again.   5) Connect the tools you already use. CRM, Stripe, Google Analytics, Meta Ads. Get API keys and allow your AIOS to pull data in and take actions for you.6) Once this foundation is there, building agents, automations and internal apps is stupidly fast. Sales pipelines, dashboards, content systems in days not quarters. 7) And no, you don’t need to be technical. Claude Code is an incredible teacher. Give it a screenshot and tell it where you’re stuck. It figures it out. You just have to be okay being uncomfortable for a bit. 8) Forget OpenClaw. It sucks mega ass compared to a proper AIOS  9) The AI agency model is juicier (and easier) than ever. People in my program are flying out to do installs and getting thousands for setups and fat retainers for ongoing work. 10) And if you are trying to sell this…stay away from enterprise. Small businesses under 100 people is where the money is without the red tape. For further reading/watching on the future of AI and business:	⁃	Jack Dorsey’s recent pod with Sequioa	⁃	My YT channel (link in bi0) What a time to be alive!!Liam 💪🏼
